assumption: Third-party credential compromise attempts are expected several times annually; lower bound assumes limited exposure, upper bound assumes elevated credential-targeting activity.
Threat actors capable of credential theft and cloud access are expected to range from moderately capable to highly capable.
Existing MFA, conditional access, vendor monitoring, PAM, and cloud logging provide material resistance but are not assumed perfect.
Derived from Threat Capability versus Control Strength rather than sampled independently.
Derived as TEF multiplied by Vulnerability for each Monte Carlo iteration.
Includes forensic investigation, containment, specialist response, legal coordination, and breach-management labor.
Includes credential reset, access remediation, restoration, validation, and temporary operational disruption.
Includes legal review, patient notification, external counsel, breach response administration, and contractual investigation.
Regulatory, reputational, or customer-related secondary impacts do not occur in every loss event.
Represents uncertain regulatory penalties, investigation costs, corrective action, and jurisdiction-dependent exposure.
Represents customer attrition, delayed contracts, trust degradation, communications, and commercial response.
Represents supplier dispute, contractual recovery effort, replacement cost, and external assurance requirements.
